items.text: Inventory all internet-facing applications, including peripheral systems: partner and supplier portals, mobile backends, employee applications, sales-support systems, legacy services, third-party integrations, and applications created across different business units.

Restrict cloud administration, network device management, application publishing interfaces (Kudu/SCM endpoints), hypervisors, backup platforms, and other sensitive services to trusted networks, private connectivity, or dedicated administrative paths.
Disable basic publishing authentication where not required; restrict access to deployment and publishing credentials; restrict SCM access to approved management networks or deployment infrastructure.
Consider deployment models such as run-from-package that reduce direct modification of deployed application files.
Establish governance around public IP allocation; require architecture review before workloads or management interfaces are exposed directly to the internet.
Move enterprise applications behind Zero Trust access solutions to eliminate external exposure where feasible.
Apply least privilege to multi-tenant application permissions and consent grants.
Monitor credential additions, privilege assignments, and anomalous app-only activity, especially for applications with high-privilege permissions and scopes.

Review every Microsoft 365 tenant where affected ConnectWise applications are or were installed or authorized, even if the integration is no longer in use; search by application ID rather than display name.
Review successful and failed service-principal sign-ins separately; investigate unfamiliar sources and activity outside expected vendor infrastructure (do not limit review to published IPs).

Review Microsoft Entra audit records for: application/service-principal credential additions; new applications, service principals, and owners; app-role assignments and consent grants; privileged role assignments; changes to users, groups, authentication methods, and Conditional Access. If suspicious activity is confirmed, revoke unnecessary permissions and rotate credentials.

Require certificate-manager or CA approval for higher-risk enrollment scenarios; enable Extended Protection for Authentication on CA web interfaces where supported; monitor unusual certificate enrollment involving privileged users or unexpected requesting systems.

Put guardrails around high-impact business APIs: rate limits, recipient limits, transaction thresholds, abuse controls appropriate to function; alert when an application operates materially outside normal volume.

On partner and employee portals, alert on sequential lookups and unusually high numbers of records accessed per session; apply rate limits to affected endpoints; enforce server-side authorization for access to customer records; limit responses to fields required for the operation.
Avoid returning detailed stack traces, compiler messages, SQL errors, internal paths, or framework details to unauthenticated users; keep detailed troubleshooting information in internal logs.

Review application configurations, environment variables, infrastructure-as-code, deployment scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and databases for embedded secrets; implement continuous scanning of repositories, container images, build artifacts, and pipelines for exposed secrets; rotate exposed credentials promptly.

Preserve available Microsoft Entra sign-in and audit records, Microsoft Purview Audit records, SIEM data, and previously configured Microsoft Graph telemetry; do not delay urgent containment while waiting for exports.

Review activity starting from at least October 1, 2026 for ConnectWise-related activity; extend service-principal sign-in review and investigate earlier related activity, including failed authentications and volume anomalies.
If suspicious activity is confirmed, have an appropriately authorized responder remove confirmed unauthorized credentials, grants, owners, assignments, and identities after preserving evidence.

Keep affected ConnectWise application connections disabled until ConnectWise provides formal restoration instructions; do not delete enterprise applications as a first response (preserve configuration and evidence before irreversible changes).
